source_text:
Look at what our schools and public institutions are coming to. During a graduation ceremony in Jaipur, right in front of the Deputy Chief Minister, a student chose to make a public protest about administrative issues while receiving her degree. This is a complete breakdown of basic respect and decorum. Instead of carrying herself with dignity on a day meant to honor achievement and tradition, she turned a solemn milestone into a platform for grievance. 

While the progressive crowd praises this kind of disruptive behavior as a bold statement, it is plainly a sign of entitlement and a lack of proper discipline. When the young lose respect for authority and the proper channels of order, chaos follows. The university administration is right to stay silent and refuse to reward this grandstanding. It is long past time we restore basic standards of decorum and personal responsibility in our schools.

This is about systemic institutional failure forcing students to use whatever platform they have left to demand accountability. For too long, traditional institutions have demanded blind obedience and silent compliance, shielding bureaucratic mismanagement behind hollow traditions of solemn milestones.

When the administration stays silent and refuses to address these grievances, it just shows their utter contempt for the student body and institutional reform. We need to stand with those who challenge unjust systems, not lecture them about tone and decorum while ignoring the structural injustices they face every single day.

Folks, once again we see the establishment and the defenders of entrenched authority panicking the moment a marginalized voice speaks truth to power. Look at what happened during a graduation ceremony in Jaipur, right in front of the Deputy Chief Minister. A student had the profound courage to make a public protest about administrative issues while receiving her degree. 

This isn't about a lack of decorum or respect, no matter how much the elites try to spin it that way to protect the status quo. This is about systemic institutional failure forcing students to use whatever platform they have left to demand accountability. For too long, traditional institutions have demanded blind obedience and silent compliance, shielding bureaucratic mismanagement behind hollow traditions of solemn milestones. 

The establishment defenders are crying about entitlement and a lack of proper discipline, desperate to maintain hierarchical control over young people who refuse to be silenced. When the administration stays silent and refuses to address these grievances, it just shows their utter contempt for the student body and institutional reform. We need to stand with those who challenge unjust systems, not lecture them about tone and decorum while ignoring the structural injustices they face every single day.
